newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault warns on commercial vehicle result.
newsitem.headline: Renault warns on commercial vehicle result.

text.p: Renault said in a statement on Friday that "the negative contribution from the commercial vehicles division will be considerably more pronounced than anticipated".

The Commercial Vehicles Division, which includes Renault VI (Vehicules Industriels) and Mack Trucks, reported sales for the first nine months of the year down 10.26 percent to 21.752 billion francs from 24.242 billion in the same period of 1995.
It reported total consolidated sales for the group of 135.778 billion francs, down from 136.999 billion last time.

"Confronted with a deterioration in the heavy-duty truck market in the United States, where sales dropped by 15 percent from the first nine months of 1995, Mack Trucks strengthened its position, attaining a market share of 11.8 percent for the first nine months against 11.5 percent a year earlier," it said.

"In Europe, where the market was undergoing a trend reversal -- a virtual stagnation of registrations and a sharp decline in orders for all makes -- Renault VI showed a slight decline in market share for vehicles over five tonnes, to 11 percent from 11.2 percent in the first nine months of 1995," it said.
"In this context, the Commercial Vehicles Division reported revenues of 21,752 million francs for the first nine months of the year," a drop of 10.26 percent, it said.
"For the third quarter of 1996, the contribution of the Commercial Vehicles division to consolidated revenues was 6,358 million, a drop of 10 percent from the 1995 period," it said.

"The Commercial Vehicles Division will have to cope with depressed markets in both Europe and the United States. The efforts initiated in the area of cost reductions will not suffice to offset the negative influences of a difficult pricing environment and transition phase in the product line, with the launch of the Premium, as well as changes to emission standards in Europe.
